title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: Britain’s government has issued a response to the 2020 Committee report on artificial intelligence and public standards, outlining its plans to strengthen AI governance. The reply stresses the need for robust, ethical and transparent AI practices, regulatory safeguards, and close collaboration with industry and academia.

title: EM on EU Regulation 2024/1689 on Artificial Intelligence
description: The government's summary of an EU regulation laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence and amending several Regulations and Directives.
summary: The document explains the EU regulation 2024/1689 that establishes common rules for artificial intelligence across the European Union. It also updates and amends other EU regulations and directives to align with these new AI rules.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is setting out how it will manage the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector. This guidance was prepared in response to a request from the Secretaries of State for Education, Science, Innovation and Technology, and Business and Trade.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report evaluates how copyright‑protected works are used to train AI systems and examines the legal and economic impacts of that practice. It offers recommendations to balance creators’ rights with the benefits of AI innovation.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has issued a formal response to the Lords Select Committee’s report “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency,” outlining how it plans to tackle the risks and benefits of artificial intelligence. It stresses that the government will take proactive steps, including new regulations and investment in AI, to keep the country ahead of potential challenges.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document outlines the purpose, scope, and responsibilities of the committee tasked with reviewing artificial intelligence in relation to public standards, detailing how the review will be conducted and what it aims to achieve. It also includes a FAQ section that clarifies the committee’s role, timeline, and expected outcomes.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry into how Artificial Intelligence should be governed. Their submission likely outlines policy recommendations or concerns about AI governance and regulation.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The policy explores how artificial intelligence changes the way medical products are regulated, focusing on risks, benefits, and ethical concerns. It outlines steps to apply the AI White Paper principles—such as safety, transparency, and accountability—to create clear, effective rules for AI‑driven medical technologies.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: This document outlines the Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy, aiming to make our defence organization the most effective, efficient, trusted and influential AI leader among similarly sized organisations worldwide. It sets a vision for using AI to boost defence capabilities and strengthen our global standing.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport AI Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will work with the transport sector to use artificial intelligence to improve services and increase efficiency. It also outlines steps to identify, assess and manage the risks of AI, ensuring safety, fairness and accountability while encouraging innovation.
